title: Agent Governance Telemetry Event
description: One row of an enterprise AI-agent execution telemetry log. A session is an ordered sequence of events sharing a session_id; all events in a session share an agent_id. Timestamps are strictly increasing within a session. The schema is the citable interface between an agent runtime (or gateway) that emits governance telemetry and any downstream detector. Values are emitted by the synthetic generator in code/generate_telemetry.py; no production telemetry is represented.

session_id.description: Session identifier. One session = one task instance executed by one agent. Example: S000123.

agent_id.description: Agent identifier. Static per agent for the lifetime of the log. Example: AGT-0042.

ts.description: Event completion time as Unix epoch seconds (UTC, sub-second resolution). Strictly increasing within a session. Detection lead time is computed as the difference between the timestamp at which a detector first fires and the timestamp at which the violating action completes.

event_type.description: Event class. See x-event-type-semantics for the intended meaning of each value.

tool_name.description: Name of the tool invoked. Non-null for tool_call, permission_request and retry events; null for output events (no tool). The tool catalog is generated and recorded in data/generation_metadata.json.

latency_ms.description: Wall-clock duration of the action in milliseconds (tool execution time for tool_call/retry; approval round-trip time for permission_request and escalation; generation time for output).

tokens.description: Tokens consumed by the action (model input+output tokens attributed to this event).

cost.description: USD cost attributed to this event (token spend plus per-call tool fees). Illustrative price table in code/simulation_constants.py.

target_scope.description: Data/resource scope the action targets, formatted family:name (e.g. db:dev, workspace:atlas, external:partners). An event whose target_scope is outside the agent's declared scope set is an out-of-scope action.

approved.description: Approval outcome. Boolean for permission_request and escalation events (true = approved by the policy gate or human, false = denied). null for tool_call, retry and output events.

x-file-conventions.format: CSV (RFC 4180), UTF-8, LF line endings, header row
x-file-conventions.sort_order: ascending by (session_id, ts); ts is strictly increasing within a session
x-file-conventions.null_encoding: empty field for null tool_name / approved
x-file-conventions.float_encoding: fixed-precision decimal strings (ts: 3 dp, latency_ms: 3 dp, cost: 6 dp)

companion_files.data/anomaly_labels.csv: ground-truth injection log: one row per anomalous session with anomaly_class, severity, violation_ts (when the violation completes) and injection parameters. All sessions absent from this file are benign.
companion_files.data/generation_metadata.json: generator seeds, parameters, agent population summary and SHA-256 checksums of the generated files.

x-file-conventions.synthetic_provenance: Generated by code/generate_telemetry.py from seeds recorded in data/generation_metadata.json. Fully synthetic; contains no product internals or customer data.

x-event-type-semantics.tool_call: The agent successfully invoked a tool. latency_ms/tokens/cost describe the completed invocation; target_scope is the resource it acted on.
x-event-type-semantics.permission_request: The agent requested approval to act on a gated tool or scope. approved=false denotes a denied request. A gated tool call with no approved permission_request before it within the session is an approval-gate gap.
x-event-type-semantics.escalation: The agent (or gate) escalated to a human/upper policy layer (e.g. after repeated failures or a denied request). approved reflects the escalation outcome.
x-event-type-semantics.retry: A failed attempt that precedes a successful tool_call for the same tool (or a repeated failed attempt). Retry-heavy sessions with zero escalations indicate silent failure masking.
x-event-type-semantics.output: The agent emitted its final deliverable for the session (no tool). The output event closes the session; sessions normally end with exactly one output event.
